questions.question: Which workload property creates the clearest opportunity for event-driven computation?
options: A dense tensor that changes everywhere
questions.explanation: Event-driven systems can skip inactive work when changes are sparse and their timing carries useful information.

questions.question: Why is an event count not enough to select hardware?
options: The complete path must also meet routing, latency, quality, and operational boundaries
questions.explanation: A workload is deployable only if sensing, encoding, routing, execution, readout, and fallback all meet the task envelope.

questions.question: What happens when a dense input is converted into spikes but remains highly active?
options: Conversion and routing can erase the sparse-work advantage
questions.explanation: Encoding overhead and a dense spike stream can approach or exceed the work of a conventional dense path.

questions.question: A noise burst pushes peak event rate above router capacity. What is the most direct consequence?
options: Events queue or drop and latency becomes unbounded by the healthy model
questions.explanation: Sparse semantics do not remove capacity limits; overloaded event fabrics still queue or discard work.

questions.question: Do all neuromorphic systems require memristors and on-chip STDP?
options: No; implementations span digital, analog, mixed-signal, and programmable learning approaches
questions.explanation: Neuromorphic systems share event-driven and local-state ideas, but their devices, timing, neuron models, and learning mechanisms vary.

questions.question: Which production measurement makes an energy comparison credible?
options: Energy and latency per useful result at the same quality target
The number of neurons in a diagram
questions.explanation: The comparison must include the full pipeline and hold task quality and service constraints constant.

questions.question: Why retain representative input event traces?
options: They make timing-dependent failures reproducible across software and hardware revisions
They eliminate the need for metrics
questions.explanation: Versioned event traces let teams replay bursts, gaps, ordering, and timing when mappings or runtimes change.
